messages:
lin: heads up — noticed long-running requests with >20k tokens slowly leak memory over hours. profiler points at KV cache fragmentation, not obvious leak in references. dump attached below.

sophie: ugh, seen this before in sims. can you paste the profiler snippet? :thinking:

lin: sure — short dump from `kv_inspect` on the heavy worker: 
```
KV cache total: 28.7GB
allocated slabs: 31
total holes: 2.1GB (8.2%)
largest hole: 256MB
avg fragment size: 48KB
active entries: 7.2M
reusable_fwd: 1.1M, tombstones: 42k
compaction_runs: 0 (since boot)
```

lin: latency also creeps: baseline P95 120ms -> 180ms after ~6h under long-context replay. CPU profile shows extra memcpy + page faults during KV lookup.

ana: typo: did you mean ana? :)

lin: yes, sorry — ana.

ana: thx. can you run `./kv_tool profile --holes --compact-sim` and post the simulation output? curious whether compaction cost spikes.

lin: ran quick sim, results: 
```
compact-sim: try_merge_slots -> 1.8s per 100MB reclaimed
incremental-pass: 120ms per 8MB reclaimed
stop-the-world compact: 3.2s pause to reclaim 1.2GB
```

lin: TL;DR: big reclaim is expensive and causes pausey behavior. incremental pass looks promising but current allocator fragmentation prevents good locality.

sophie: what's the allocator today? slab with fixed 16KB blocks and buddy-style coalescing at power-of-two extents?

lin: yes — 16KB base_block, chunks can grow in powers of 2 up to 1MB. we see many mid-sized fragments (~32-128KB) that are not coalescing because adjacent live entries pin neighbors. also tombstones not recycled aggressively.

mike: have we tried smaller base block (4KB) and then grouping into larger meta-slabs? that reduces internal fragmentation but increases metadata overhead — might hurt lookup speed.

lin: we ran a microbench: switching to 4KB reduced hole bytes by ~30% at cost of ~6% CPU on hot path. but P50 unaffected. main problem is long-lived KV entries created by long contexts.

ana: can we do workload-aware binning: small-value pool (<=16KB) and large-value pool (>16KB) with different compaction heuristics? small pool gets aggressive reuse, large pool uses tombstone-delay to avoid thrash.

lin: that was one of our proposals. pros: fewer cross-size fragmentation cases. cons: more codepaths. Also need to measure cache hit/latency for prefix-cache.

david: from model side — some prompts append incremental system tokens causing many small KV inserts. we can batch merges client-side to reduce tiny writes to KV. simple mitigation might reduce churn by ~20-30% on our logs.

lin: good call — I'll add a server-side option to coalesce small consecutive writes in the request processing path before committing to KV cache. low risk.

sophie: about compaction: proposal sketch — incremental background scrubbing that: 1) tracks fragmentation ratio per slab, 2) schedules light passes on slabs with frag_ratio>0.12, 3) moves entries out of low-density slabs into freshly allocated coalesced slabs, 4) frees old slabs. do it with quota-limited bandwidth and preemption (yield every 50ms).

lin: exactly. we tested yield=50ms and it cut steady-state holes by ~60% over 2h with <2% extra CPU and no P95 regressions. details: `scrubber.bandwidth=8MB/s`, `scrubber.yield_ms=50`.

mike: how to handle ordering / KV cache consistency while moving objects? we need atomic pointer swap or epoched read path. current cache read path expects stable slab pointers.

lin: plan is epoched handles: writers update through CAS to the entry header, readers check stamp and retry if stale. cost ~one compare and branch in hotpath. microbench shows ~1.5% lookup overhead. worth it, IMO.

ana: locking is scary for high QPS. ensure we have metrics per-operation for retried reads. also add a `compact_disabled` per-tenant flag for Dedicated to avoid surprises.

lin: yep — will gate behind feature flag and admin toggle. also add rollback if scrubber induces >2% P95 regression during canary.

david: can we simulate a canary with heavy long-context replay? I can produce a replay trace from staging that mimics 50k-token dialogues.

lin: please do, david. I'll wire the scrubber into a canary cluster and run replay.

ops-bot: deploy scheduled: canary/kvc-scrub-sim -> 2450 -> 2489012500 (ETA 5m) :rotating_light:

sophie: also let's add a new metric `kv_frag_ratio` (per-slab) and `kv_reclaimed_bytes/sec` so we can alert if fragmentation climbs.

lin: creating RFC PR with design + tests + perf numbers. I'll include: benchmark harness, `kv_tool` sim scripts, and fallback plan (disable scrubber).

mike: timeline suggestion: prototype in 2w, smoke canary in 1w after that, full rollout 3w after prototype if stable.

lin: cool. Action items: 
- david: provide long-context trace for replay (ETA 48h)
- lin: PR for scrubber + metrics + feature flag (ETA 2w)
- sophie: write canary runbook + alert thresholds (ETA 3d)
- ana: prepare Dedicated gating toggle + compliance note (ETA 4d)

lin: thanks all. will post updates in this thread as I push benchmarks. :thumbsup:

sophie: :rocket:

ops-bot: canary started (task id kvc-2489012500) — tracking logs at https://canary.internal/redwood/kvc-2489012500
